purpose: Triage-gates Step 4's 'successor before archive' rule. Two long-standing tensions describe a live exposure that a role created since covers structurally. Archiving them alone drops the exposure, because no other record carries it. The successor must be written on the covering role, citing the originals, BEFORE either archive. Modelled on ten_343f2946 and ten_564abcab, superseded by the creation of an Information Security Officer role (issue #120).

roles.name: Technology Circle
roles.purpose: Systems the organization can depend on without watching them
accountabilities: Holding the coherence of the organization's technical estate

roles.name: Platform Operations
roles.purpose: Infrastructure nobody has to think about
accountabilities: Running the deployment and monitoring pipeline

roles.name: Information Security Officer
roles.purpose: Exposure is owned before it is discovered
accountabilities: Reviewing and approving third-party access to organizational data
Maintaining the joiner-mover-leaver process for system credentials
Holding the register of known security exposures and their owners

tensions.body: Third-party tools get connected to our production data without anyone reviewing what they can read. Two vendors currently hold broad read access that nobody approved and nobody reviews. Platform Operations runs the pipeline but does not own the access decision, so the review keeps not happening and the access keeps accumulating.

When someone leaves, their credentials stay live until somebody happens to notice. There is no owner for revocation and no list of what needs revoking, so at least three departed contributors still have working logins to systems holding customer data.
